text:
Noah: Quick onboarding qs — I start 2025-12-29 and had a few items: 1) relocation stipend (I was told $2,000)  is that paid on first paycheck or as separate reimbursement? 2) do we have commuter pre-tax benefits and what's the enrollment cutoff? 3) will I get paid for the company holiday on Jan 1 even though I started Dec 29? 4) who do I upload receipts to for the relocation expenses?

Aisha: Welcome Noah! :wave: TL;DR: relocation stipend is usually paid as a one-time reimbursement (taxable by default unless there's an exception), commuter benefits require enrollment in the commuter portal by the 20th of the month to apply to the next month, Jan 1 holiday pay is prorated for very new hires based on start date & workdays, and receipts go in Expensify under "Relocation". I can walk you through details.

Noah: Thanks — can you confirm the tax piece? I thought relocation might be non-taxable sometimes.

Aisha: Right — federal law changed; most reimbursed relocation amounts are treated as taxable income unless the expense meets very specific conditions and we pre-authorize it. Our default is to include the $2,000 stipend on your paystub as taxable income on the payroll run that processes the reimbursement. If you think you qualify for non-taxable treatment, submit the Moving Authorization Form via the HR portal and tag it for "tax review" BEFORE we reimburse.

BenefitsBot: Stipend note: Relocation stipend $2,000 recorded 2025-12-15. Reimbursement processing ETA: next payroll cycle after approvals. Taxable by default; submit Moving Authorization Form to request non-taxable review.

Noah: Got it. For receipts: is a receipt + boarding pass enough? I have receipts for moving van and an Airbnb for 3 nights.

Aisha: Yes, upload receipts to Expensify -> New Expense -> Category: Relocation -> attach PDFs/photos. For lodging include dates and location, for movers include itemized invoice. Put a short note about reason (e.g., "new hire relocation 12/2025") and select reimbursement method ACH. Finance approves and then payroll includes the payment. Expect ~5-10 business days post-approval.

Noah: About commuter: I plan to use transit. How do I enroll and does it debit pre-tax from my paycheck?

Aisha: We use a Commuter Benefits vendor (link in benefits portal). Enrollment path: Benefits Portal -> Perks & Commuter -> Enroll. Enrollment by the 20th of the month takes effect for the following month deductions. Deductions are pre-tax up to the IRS monthly limit for transit/parking. If you enroll mid-month you'll be prorated. There's also a monthly reload option for monthly pass purchases.

PayrollOps: Payroll cutoff reminder: cutoff is every Friday 5:00 PM PT. Next payroll cutoff: 2025-12-26 17:00 PT. Reimbursements or stipend approvals received before cutoff will be included in next pay run. Holiday pay/pto proration rules applied at payroll processing.

Noah: And the Jan 1 holiday 9 I start Dec 29 (Mon) 9 will I get paid for the holiday or is it pro-rated out?

Aisha: For U.S. salaried employees: holidays that occur within your first partial pay period are pro-rated based on the company's holiday pro-rata rule (calculated by calendar days in that pay period). In practice if your start is Dec 29 and Jan 1 is within the first pay period, you'll typically get the pro-rated holiday pay (not always the full day). If you want an exact dollar estimate I can run the calc for your band and salary.

Noah: One last: if I need the stipend to land before I pay movers (week of 12/22), is there an expedited option?

Aisha: We can fast-track reimbursements in emergency cases. Email people-ops@redwood.inference with receipts and explain urgency; mark the expense "Relocation - expedite" in Expensify. We'll flag it to finance; approval + payroll cutoff timing still apply so faster isn't guaranteed but we do escalate urgent relocation cases.

Noah: Perfect. Thanks so much! I'll upload receipts now and enroll in commuter portal.

Aisha: Welcome aboard, Noah! Ping me if you want the exact holiday proration calc. :tada:
